# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_mcp_reference.py. Do not edit this page by hand: edit scripts/mcp_tool_areas.json or the server's descriptors and build it again. -->

Every tool of the OHLCX MCP server (version 1.1.0), grouped by area: 147 tools. Each tool has one line here and its arguments below. Tool names, argument names, types and argument descriptions are the server's own.

For what the server can and cannot do, start with the [overview](../overview.md). The same list in the server's own order is the [generated tool list](README.md); the machine-readable index is [index.json](index.json).

## How to read this page

**Kind** is the hint the server sends with the tool, which MCP clients use to decide when to ask the user:

| Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Read | Marked read-only. It changes nothing. |
| Write | Changes something. Marked not destructive. |
| Write, destructive | Changes or deletes something, or changes what a strategy does. Marked destructive: clients should ask the user first. |
| Write, no hint | Changes something and carries no hint. Treat it as a write and ask the user first. |

**Availability** says who is offered the tool. A tool you are not offered is not in the tool list at all.

| Availability | Tools | Listed when |
|---|---|---|
| Everyone | 4 | Always, also without a signed-in user. |
| Signed in | 119 | The request has a signed-in user. |
| Signed in, OHLCX Pro | 2 | Signed in, on OHLCX Pro, where orders are routed for the signed-in user. |
| Signed in, server backtests on | 5 | Signed in, and the app has server backtests switched on. |
| Signed in, support desk connected | 4 | Signed in, and the app is connected to the support desk. |
| Admin | 13 | The signed-in user is an admin. |

## Health and assistants

`ping` checks the connection. The two assistant tools run the same assistants as the OHLCX app and return plain text, not JSON. They call a language model, so they are slower than the data tools and their answers vary. For data you intend to process, call the data tools directly.

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`ping`](#ping) | Health check. Returns the text `pong`. | Read | Everyone |
| [`run-support-agent`](#run-support-agent) | Ask the support assistant, which answers from the knowledge base only. Returns plain text. | Read | Everyone |
| [`run-trading-agent`](#run-trading-agent) | Ask the trading assistant, which reads the signed-in user's strategies, accounts and the knowledge base. Returns plain text. | Write, no hint | Signed in |

### `ping`

Health check. Returns the text `pong`.

Read. Everyone.

No arguments.

### `run-support-agent`

Ask the support assistant, which answers from the knowledge base only. Returns plain text.

Read. Everyone.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | yes | User message / question for the support agent. |

### `run-trading-agent`

Ask the trading assistant, which reads the signed-in user's strategies, accounts and the knowledge base. Returns plain text.

Write, no hint. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | yes | User message for the trading assistant. |

## Knowledge base

Reading the knowledge base needs no sign-in. Writing it is for admins.

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`search-knowledge-base`](#search-knowledge-base) | Search or list knowledge base articles, optionally by area or by text. | Read | Everyone |
| [`get-knowledge-base-article`](#get-knowledge-base-article) | Fetch one article by its slug. | Read | Everyone |
| [`create-knowledge-base-article`](#create-knowledge-base-article) | Create an article. | Write, no hint | Admin |
| [`update-knowledge-base-article`](#update-knowledge-base-article) | Update an article by id. | Write, no hint | Admin |
| [`delete-knowledge-base-article`](#delete-knowledge-base-article) | Delete an article by id. | Write, destructive | Admin |

### `search-knowledge-base`

Search or list knowledge base articles, optionally by area or by text.

Read. Everyone.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `area` | string | no | Optional. Filter by area (e.g. dashboard, orders, overview). |
| `q` | string | no | Optional. Search in title and content. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most articles to return, 1 to 200 (default 50). |
| `offset` | integer | no | Rows to skip first, 0 to 100000 (default 0): give next_offset from the previous answer to read on. |

### `get-knowledge-base-article`

Fetch one article by its slug.

Read. Everyone.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slug` | string | yes | The article slug (e.g. overview, dashboard, orders). |

### `create-knowledge-base-article`

Create an article.

Write, no hint. Admin.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `payload` | object | no | Article attributes (title, slug, area, content, etc.). |

### `update-knowledge-base-article`

Update an article by id.

Write, no hint. Admin.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The article ID to update. |
| `payload` | object | no | Article attributes to update. |

### `delete-knowledge-base-article`

Delete an article by id.

Write, destructive. Admin.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The article ID to delete. |

## Accounts

Every tool here names an account by its account id and shows its number only as a masked label. Output shapes, the forms `account_id` accepts and the refusal for an account that is not yours are on [Accounts and identifiers](../accounts.md).

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`list-accounts`](#list-accounts) | The user's linked brokerage accounts: each account's id, masked label, type, flags and balances. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-accounts-balances`](#get-accounts-balances) | Daily balance history of every linked account in one call. The last 30 days unless `days` says otherwise. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-account-balance`](#get-account-balance) | Daily balance history of one account. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-account-growth`](#get-account-growth) | Growth data for one account. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-account-pnl`](#get-account-pnl) | Profit and loss data for one account. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-account-pnl-history`](#get-account-pnl-history) | Realized profit and loss over time for one account, for a period or between two dates. Needs the user's consent to P&L sync, given in the app. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-account-pnl-symbols`](#get-account-pnl-symbols) | Realized profit and loss by symbol for one account, for a period or between two dates. Needs the user's consent to P&L sync, given in the app. | Read | Signed in |
| [`list-account-cash-transfers`](#list-account-cash-transfers) | Deposits and withdrawals of one account, for a period or between two dates. | Read | Signed in |

### `list-accounts`

The user's linked brokerage accounts: each account's id, masked label, type, flags and balances.

|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | Most accounts to return, 1 to 100 (default 100). |

## Orders (read-only)

These two tools read broker orders. No tool places, changes or cancels an order. See [Accounts and identifiers](../accounts.md#orders).

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`list-orders`](#list-orders) | Broker orders placed between two dates, across the linked accounts or for one. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-order`](#get-order) | One broker order by its id, with its legs, fills and status. | Read | Signed in |

### `list-orders`

Broker orders placed between two dates, across the linked accounts or for one.

Read. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start_date` | string | yes | First day, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `end_date` | string | yes | Last day, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `account_id` | string or integer | no | Only this account's orders. The brokerage account: the id list-accounts gives. |
| `status` | string | no | Only orders in this broker status, e.g. FILLED, WORKING, CANCELED. |
| `max_results` | integer | no | Most orders to return, 1 to 500 (default 100). |

### `get-order`

One broker order by its id, with its legs, fills and status.

Read. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | string or integer | yes | The brokerage account: the id list-accounts gives. |
| `order_id` | string | yes | The broker's order ID. |

## Strategies: reading

A strategy can be read only by the user who owns it. Paging and period filters are on [Limits and paging](../limits-and-paging.md).

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`list-strategies`](#list-strategies) | The user's strategies. Up to 50 without arguments; `page` or `per_page` asks for the paged list. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy`](#get-strategy) | One strategy by id, with its order accounts under `routing`. | Read | Signed in |
| [`search-strategies`](#search-strategies) | Search the user's strategies by symbol. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy-activities`](#get-strategy-activities) | Activities of one strategy. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy-conditions`](#get-strategy-conditions) | Conditions of one strategy. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy-statistics`](#get-strategy-statistics) | One strategy's trade statistics (counts, win rate, profit and loss) for a period. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategies-statistics`](#get-strategies-statistics) | Trade statistics across all of the user's strategies for a period. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy-performance`](#get-strategy-performance) | One strategy's performance over time (the profit and loss series) for a period. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategies-performance`](#get-strategies-performance) | Performance over time across all of the user's strategies for a period. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy-timeline`](#get-strategy-timeline) | What a strategy did, day by day, over the last days (7 by default). | Read | Signed in |
| [`list-strategy-signals`](#list-strategy-signals) | The signals a strategy has raised, 100 per page. | Read | Signed in |
| [`list-strategy-trades`](#list-strategy-trades) | The trades a strategy has taken, 100 per page. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-strategy-flags`](#get-strategy-flags) | The flags a strategy's conditions have raised, 100 per page. | Read | Signed in |

### `list-strategies`

The user's strategies. Up to 50 without arguments; `page` or `per_page` asks for the paged list.

## Strategies: changing

Read the `ohlcx://strategy-settings` resource before you create a strategy or change its settings. A deployed strategy refuses the changes marked below with "Retain the strategy before changing it.": retain it first. See [Strategies and order routing](../strategy-routing.md#the-deployed-lock).

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`create-strategy`](#create-strategy) | Create a strategy. `payload` needs the fields listed in the `ohlcx://strategy-settings` resource. | Write, no hint | Signed in |
| [`update-strategy`](#update-strategy) | Update a strategy's definition by id. Refused while the strategy is deployed. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`delete-strategy`](#delete-strategy) | Delete a strategy by id. Refused while the strategy is deployed. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`duplicate-strategy`](#duplicate-strategy) | Duplicate a strategy. | Write, no hint | Signed in |
| [`update-strategy-settings`](#update-strategy-settings) | Update one section of a strategy's settings; each section is validated on its own. Refused while the strategy is deployed. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`set-strategy-schedule`](#set-strategy-schedule) | Set the days and hours a strategy is allowed to run. Times are New York time. Refused while the strategy is deployed. | Write | Signed in |
| [`clear-strategy-conditions-readings`](#clear-strategy-conditions-readings) | Clear the reading of every condition of a strategy. Refused while the strategy is deployed. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`clear-strategy-data`](#clear-strategy-data) | Delete all of a strategy's signals, trades or flags. Cannot be undone. Flags: refused while deployed. Signals: refused only while deployed, real and with orders on. Trades: never refused. | Write, destructive | Signed in |

### `create-strategy`

Create a strategy. `payload` needs the fields listed in the `ohlcx://strategy-settings` resource.

Write, no hint. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `payload` | object | yes | Strategy attributes: name, symbol, direction (buy, sell, both), timeframe, status, deployed, is_demo, signals_on, trades_on, orders_on, notify_signals, notify_trades, notify_orders. |

### `update-strategy`

Update a strategy's definition by id. Refused while the strategy is deployed.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The strategy ID to update. |
| `payload` | object | no | Strategy attributes to update. |

### `delete-strategy`

Delete a strategy by id. Refused while the strategy is deployed.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The strategy ID to delete. |

### `duplicate-strategy`

Duplicate a strategy.

Write, no hint. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | string | yes | The strategy ID to duplicate. |

### `update-strategy-settings`

Update one section of a strategy's settings; each section is validated on its own. Refused while the strategy is deployed.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `section` | string | yes | The section to update. Allowed: `risk-management`, `allocation`, `sizing-ordering`, `order-flow`, `order-cancelation`, `name`, `symbol`, `direction`, `timeframe`. |
| `settings` | object | yes | The section's fields and their new values. |

### `set-strategy-schedule`

Set the days and hours a strategy is allowed to run. Times are New York time. Refused while the strategy is deployed.

Write. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `schedule_enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the schedule is in force. |
| `schedule_days` | array | yes | Days of the week it may run, as numbers 1 to 7. |
| `schedule_start_time` | string | yes | Start time, HH:MM (24-hour). |
| `schedule_end_time` | string | yes | End time, HH:MM (24-hour). |

### `clear-strategy-conditions-readings`

Clear the reading of every condition of a strategy. Refused while the strategy is deployed.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | string | yes | The strategy ID. |

### `clear-strategy-data`

Delete all of a strategy's signals, trades or flags. Cannot be undone. Flags: refused while deployed. Signals: refused only while deployed, real and with orders on. Trades: never refused.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `target` | string | yes | What to clear: signals, trades or flags. Allowed: `signals`, `trades`, `flags`. |

## Strategies: order routing and running

These tools decide whether a strategy runs, whether it sends orders, and to which accounts. They are walked through in order on [Strategies and order routing](../strategy-routing.md). Confirm each of them with the user first.

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`list-strategy-accounts`](#list-strategy-accounts) | The linked accounts as a strategy's orders can be routed to them: account id, masked label, whether the account can receive orders now and, if not, the reason. | Read | Signed in, OHLCX Pro |
| [`set-strategy-accounts`](#set-strategy-accounts) | Choose the order accounts of a strategy: mode `selected` with account ids, or mode `all`. Never switches orders on or off. Refused while the strategy is deployed. | Write, destructive | Signed in, OHLCX Pro |
| [`set-strategy-flag`](#set-strategy-flag) | Switch signals, trades or orders (or their notifications) on or off, or toggle them. On and toggle are refused while the strategy is deployed; off always works. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`set-strategy-status`](#set-strategy-status) | Switch a strategy on or off. On is refused while the strategy is deployed; off always works. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`deploy-strategy`](#deploy-strategy) | Deploy a strategy, so that the engine evaluates it. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`retain-strategy`](#retain-strategy) | Retain a strategy: take it out of evaluation, so that it can be changed again. With `stop` true it also switches orders, trades and signals off. | Write, destructive | Signed in |

### `list-strategy-accounts`

The linked accounts as a strategy's orders can be routed to them: account id, masked label, whether the account can receive orders now and, if not, the reason.

Read. Signed in, OHLCX Pro.

No arguments.

### `set-strategy-accounts`

Choose the order accounts of a strategy: mode `selected` with account ids, or mode `all`. Never switches orders on or off. Refused while the strategy is deployed.

Write, destructive. Signed in, OHLCX Pro.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `mode` | string | yes | "selected": only the accounts in account_ids. "all": every linked account that can receive orders when an order is sent, including accounts linked later. Allowed: `selected`, `all`. |
| `account_ids` | array of integer | no | Account ids from list-strategy-accounts (whole numbers, at most 50, each once). Required with mode "selected", where an empty list removes every account; not used with "all". |

### `set-strategy-flag`

Switch signals, trades or orders (or their notifications) on or off, or toggle them. On and toggle are refused while the strategy is deployed; off always works.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `flag` | string | yes | Which flag: signals, trades or orders. Allowed: `signals`, `trades`, `orders`. |
| `state` | string | yes | on, off or toggle. Use off to stop: toggle is refused while the strategy is deployed, off always works. Allowed: `on`, `off`, `toggle`. |
| `notifications` | boolean | no | True to switch the notifications for that flag instead of the flag itself (default false). |

### `set-strategy-status`

Switch a strategy on or off. On is refused while the strategy is deployed; off always works.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `status` | string | yes | on or off. Allowed: `on`, `off`. |

### `deploy-strategy`

Deploy a strategy, so that the engine evaluates it.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | string | yes | The strategy ID to deploy. |

### `retain-strategy`

Retain a strategy: take it out of evaluation, so that it can be changed again. With `stop` true it also switches orders, trades and signals off.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID to retain. |
| `stop` | boolean | no | True to also switch orders, trades and signals off (default false: the switches stay as they were). |

## Backtests

The first four tools read and manage saved runs. The last five start and follow server-side runs and are listed only where the app has server backtests switched on. At most three backtests may wait or run at once.

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`list-backtests`](#list-backtests) | The user's saved backtest runs, newest first, with each run's metrics. | Read | Signed in |
| [`get-backtest`](#get-backtest) | One saved run: its period, settings, what-if overrides and metrics. The trade list, equity curve and strategy snapshot come only when named in `include`. | Read | Signed in |
| [`rename-backtest`](#rename-backtest) | Rename a saved run. | Write | Signed in |
| [`delete-backtest`](#delete-backtest) | Delete a saved run. Cannot be undone. | Write, destructive | Signed in |
| [`run-backtest`](#run-backtest) | Start a server-side backtest of a strategy as it is now. It runs in the background: poll `get-backtest-job`. | Write | Signed in, server backtests on |
| [`run-backtest-sweep`](#run-backtest-sweep) | Start a parameter sweep: the strategy is backtested once for every combination of one or two settings, and the results are ranked. | Write | Signed in, server backtests on |
| [`list-backtest-jobs`](#list-backtest-jobs) | The user's server-side backtests and sweeps, newest first, with status and progress. | Read | Signed in, server backtests on |
| [`get-backtest-job`](#get-backtest-job) | One server-side job: its status, progress, and when finished the saved run's `backtest_id` (a run) or the ranked result (a sweep). | Read | Signed in, server backtests on |
| [`cancel-backtest-job`](#cancel-backtest-job) | Cancel a server-side job that is still waiting or running. | Write, destructive | Signed in, server backtests on |

### `list-backtests`

The user's saved backtest runs, newest first, with each run's metrics.

Read. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | no | Only runs of this strategy. |
| `page` | integer | no | Page number, 1 to 100000 (default 1). |
| `offset` | integer | no | Rows of the page to skip first, 0 to 24 (default 0): give next_offset from the previous answer to read the rows the size budget left out of this page. |

### `get-backtest`

One saved run: its period, settings, what-if overrides and metrics. The trade list, equity curve and strategy snapshot come only when named in `include`.

Read. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `backtest_id` | integer | yes | The saved run's ID. |
| `include` | array of string | no | Large parts to return as well: trades, equity, strategy_snapshot. Allowed: `trades`, `equity`, `strategy_snapshot`. |

### `rename-backtest`

Rename a saved run.

Write. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `backtest_id` | integer | yes | The saved run's ID. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name (up to 120 characters). |

### `delete-backtest`

Delete a saved run. Cannot be undone.

Write, destructive. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `backtest_id` | integer | yes | The saved run's ID. |

### `run-backtest`

Start a server-side backtest of a strategy as it is now. It runs in the background: poll `get-backtest-job`.

Write. Signed in, server backtests on.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `from_day` | string | yes | First day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `to_day` | string | yes | Last day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD. The period may cover at most five years. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the run (up to 120 characters). |
| `overrides` | object | no | What-if changes applied to the strategy for this run only: {strategy: {setting: value}, disabledConditionIds: [ids]}. The live strategy is not changed. |
| `run_settings` | object | no | Further run settings, as the backtest form sends them. from_day and to_day take precedence. |

### `run-backtest-sweep`

Start a parameter sweep: the strategy is backtested once for every combination of one or two settings, and the results are ranked.

Write. Signed in, server backtests on.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | yes | The strategy ID. |
| `from_day` | string | yes | First day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `to_day` | string | yes | Last day of the period, YYYY-MM-DD. The period may cover at most five years. |
| `name` | string | no | A name for the run (up to 120 characters). |
| `overrides` | object | no | What-if changes applied to the strategy for this run only: {strategy: {setting: value}, disabledConditionIds: [ids]}. The live strategy is not changed. |
| `run_settings` | object | no | Further run settings, as the backtest form sends them. from_day and to_day take precedence. |
| `axes` | array | yes | One or two settings to vary. A numeric setting: {key, from, to, step}. risk_reward: {key: "risk_reward"} tries every ratio. Keys are strategy settings such as distance_sl, distance_tp, min_distance_sl, min_distance_tp, position, capital, risk, trailing_stop_value. |
| `measure` | string | no | What to rank by (default netProfit). Allowed: `netProfit`, `profitFactor`, `sharpe`, `winRate`, `expectancy`, `returnOverDrawdown`, `maxDrawdownPct`. |
| `holdout` | boolean | no | Keep the last 30% of the period away from the search and check the best result on it (default false). |

### `list-backtest-jobs`

The user's server-side backtests and sweeps, newest first, with status and progress.

Read. Signed in, server backtests on.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategy_id` | integer | no | Only jobs of this strategy. |
| `page` | integer | no | Page number, 1 to 100000 (default 1). |
| `offset` | integer | no | Rows of the page to skip first, 0 to 24 (default 0): give next_offset from the previous answer to read the rows the size budget left out of this page. |

### `get-backtest-job`

One server-side job: its status, progress, and when finished the saved run's `backtest_id` (a run) or the ranked result (a sweep).

Read. Signed in, server backtests on.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | integer | yes | The job ID. |

### `cancel-backtest-job`

Cancel a server-side job that is still waiting or running.

Write, destructive. Signed in, server backtests on.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | integer | yes | The job ID. |

## Workspaces

Workspaces are the user's saved layouts of charts and widgets. They are saved as one document against a revision.

| Tool | What it does | Kind | Availability |

### `get-workspaces`

The user's Workspaces document, with the revision to send back when saving.

Read. Signed in.

No arguments.

Save the whole Workspaces document against a revision. If it was changed somewhere else, nothing is saved and the current state and revision come back.

Write. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |

### `screen-market-gaps`

The symbols of a market that gapped at the open, each with its size, plus the market's gap statistics for the session.

Read. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `market_id` | integer | no | The market to screen (see list-markets; default 3). |
| `gap_min_percent` | number | no | Smallest gap to report, in percent (default 2). |
| `direction` | string | no | Gap direction: up, down or both (default up). Allowed: `up`, `down`, `both`. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most gaps to return, 1 to 200 (default 50). |
| `offset` | integer | no | Rows to skip first, 0 to 100000 (default 0): give next_offset from the previous answer to read on. |

| `timeframe` | string | no | Bar timeframe (default 1Day). Allowed: `1Min`, `5Min`, `15Min`, `30Min`, `1Hour`, `4Hour`, `1Day`, `1Week`. |
| `gap_min_percent` | number | no | Smallest gap to report, in percent (default 2). |
| `direction` | string | no | Gap direction: up, down or both (default up). Allowed: `up`, `down`, `both`. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most gaps to return, 1 to 200 (default 50). |
| `offset` | integer | no | Rows to skip first, 0 to 100000 (default 0): give next_offset from the previous answer to read on. |

### `screen-technicals`

A market's symbols by their technical readings on a timeframe: moving averages, pivots and indicator signals, with the market's summary.

Read. Signed in.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
